summary: The core is laid out as a netlist of the Nintendo board, building on Katsumi Degawa's chip-level Donkey Kong design. Address decoding goes through a decoder PROM feeding instantiated 74LS138/139 decoders and a 74LS259-style latch. The sprite engine is a pipeline of per-chip registers, adders, counters and line-buffer RAMs, clocked from H-counter bits, and has nothing in common with MAME's draw_sprites loop. MAME-like or simplified parts are limited to the sprite DMA (a fixed-length copier) and the sound CPUs' address compares, and those only reproduce the memory map.

findings.signal: Address decode via decoder PROM and 74xx138/139 instances
findings.where: rtl/dkong3_adec.v:89-202 (prom5e, U_3B_1/U_3B_2, U_2A, U_3A, U_4E, U_4F)
findings.note: Chip selects come from a 5E PROM indexed by A15-A11 and cascaded logic_74xx138/139 decoders, gated by MREQ/RD/WR and a WAIT flip-flop. MAME uses address-map handler entries instead.
The Z80 WAIT comes from a 2D flip-flop fed by a VRAMBUSY signal that is clocked off H_CNT[2] and cleared by H_CNT[9]. MAME does not model this bus contention.

findings.signal: Control latch 3E with schematic signal semantics
findings.note: One addressable 8-bit latch, strobed by 4E decoder output Q5 and selected by A2-A0, drives flip, 2PSL, NMI clear, DMA RDY and CAD6/7 as plain outputs. MAME uses a separate *_w function for each address.

findings.signal: Sprite scan pipeline built from chip-named stages
findings.note: Sprite selection is done by 8-bit adder chains and a NAND of the top four sum bits, with a counter and 64x9 RAM (7M) buffering candidates, all timed by H_CNT bits. MAME instead runs a per-scanline for-loop over sprite RAM with a 16-sprite cap and gfx transpen calls.

findings.signal: Board line buffer and shift registers for sprite pixels
findings.where: rtl/dkong3_obj.v:250-358 (8CD/8EF shifters, 8B mux, 3E counter, 2EH RAM, 3K latch)
findings.note: Sprite pixels are shifted out of 74LS299-style registers into a 256x6 line buffer addressed by a loadable counter, with XOR for flip and clear-on-readback. This is the board's scan-time pipeline, not a bitmap blit.

findings.signal: Background tile path as 2114 RAM, colour PROM, shift registers, LS157 mux
findings.note: VRAM is addressed from VF_CNT[7:3] and the flipped H_CNT[8:4]. Its data indexes the 3N/3P ROMs, which load the 4P/4N shift registers; mode control comes from the 4M mux and colour from PROM 2N latched by 2M. There is no tilemap callback.

findings.signal: Per-pixel priority and palette lookup through PROMs
findings.note: Sprite-over-background choice is a 3M/3L mux on the sprite pixel bits. The result plus CAD6/7 is registered (1B/2C) and addresses the 1D/1C colour PROMs, with link CL1 selecting the PROM half. MAME precomputes the palette through res_net decoding instead.

findings.signal: Raster counters and board signal naming
findings.note: Counters produce 1H..256H, VF (V XOR flip) and blanking. The flip signal passes through an explicit INV/XOR/INV gate chain, and nets carry chip-location names (W_5F1_Q, W_6K_Q, W_8N_Q).

findings.signal: Sound board latches per chip location
findings.note: Sound command latches are modelled as 74LS374s at 4J, 4H and 5F, strobed by 4E decoder outputs. Sub-CPU reads at 4016/4017 use plain address compares, which matches the memory map and counts as neutral.
Neither the board's Z80 DMA chip nor MAME's z80dma device is modelled. A small FSM copies a hardcoded 0x19F bytes when RDY rises. This is a behavioural shortcut with no MAME decomposition.
